subject: Customer request: US-only model routing + disallow fallback (ACME)

To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Customer request: US-only model routing + disallow fallback (ACME)

Team —

ACME reached out this morning with a fairly strict ask: they want all inference for their account routed to a specific US-only model variant (we'll call it model-x-us-v1) and they do NOT want any automated fallback to other model variants or regions. Their rationale: evaluation against a fixed model family and an internal audit that requires no compute leaving US regions.

Key asks from ACME (attached: acme_data_requirements_v2.pdf):
- Enforce routing to model-x-us-v1 only (no automatic fallback).
- Ensure traffic stays in US regions (no cross-region failover).
- Provide audit logs showing model variant and region for each request.

Questions I need from engineering/product/legal before I reply to Sally:
1) Feasibility: can we implement a per-account "no-fallback + region lock + forced model" config, and how invasive is it?
2) Availability/risk: what happens during outages in us-west2/us-east1? Any way to keep customers protected if the single-region capacity is exhausted?
3) Cost/ops: estimated engineering lead time and run cost delta (reserved capacity, warm standby, etc.).
4) Compliance: what contract clauses or assurances do we need to offer?

ACME is on a potential expansion path (Deal ID DEAL-8341). Marissa — this is an active renewal/expansion conversation; we should consider whether this requires Dedicated/Private or if hosted can be made acceptable.

Can each of you send a short note on feasibility + any blocker by EOD Tuesday? I want to avoid promising anything until we have alignment.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Customer request: US-only model routing + disallow fallback (ACME)

Quick technical readout — from infra/product perspective. TL;DR: possible, but operationally risky unless we reserve capacity.

Feasibility notes:
- We can add a per-account routing flag (e.g., allow_fallback=false + region_policy=us-only + enforced_model=model-x-us-v1). Implementation would touch the routing layer and the policy store (2-3 sprints for a minimal, guarded rollout).
- Existing runtime can pin a request to a particular model binary/variant; the routing change is straightforward. Main changes are in the control plane (per-account routing rules) and the capacity planner.

Availability/risk:
- No-fallback means if model-x-us-v1 is unavailable in the customer's chosen zone, requests will queue or fail. To meet reasonable availability, ACME will need either:
  a) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) sized to their peak, or
  b) A warm-standby of the same model in another US region with manual failover (but that violates "no cross-region" if strictly enforced).
- We can implement a safelist for manual operator failover, but that would be an "operator-in-loop" exception and must be documented.

Cost estimates (rough):
- Engineering: 6–8 engineer-weeks to land safe per-account routing + UI and tests.
- Infra: if they require reserved capacity, estimate $Xk/month depending on token volume (I can model if Marissa provides traffic profile).

Observability/compliance:
- We can emit model-variant and region tags to the audit log (already present in traces; we need to surface per-request metadata to compliance exports).

Attachments: routing_config_proposal.md (proto config + rollout plan).

Risks to call out before agreeing to "no-fallback":
- Increased outage risk and possible SLA implications.
- Operational burden for manual failover if cross-region fallback is forbidden.

Happy to sync and pick a path (Dedicated pilot vs hosted config).

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Customer request: US-only model routing + disallow fallback (ACME)

Legal & security considerations — short summary.

From a compliance perspective, their request is reasonable (US-only compute + per-request audit trails) but we must be explicit about availability trade-offs in the contract. Actionable items: 
1) Contract language: add an exception clause that documents the "no-fallback" behavior, the operational consequences, and an agreed SLA (or explicit absence of SLA for cross-region failover). We should also include an emergency operator-failover process and change control for invoking it.
2) Encryption & keys: if they insist on strict US-residency of keys, we need to confirm KMS location (customer-managed key in US KMS). If they want HSM-backed keys, that's an extra product/ops discussion.
3) Audit/log exports: we can provide per-request metadata (model variant, region, request id) to an S3 bucket or shared Drive; confirm retention window.
4) SOC2/Security evidence: this request doesn't change our SOC2 stance, but it raises expectations around proof of region residency — we should provide logs and a runbook describing controls.

Finally, the "no-fallback" requirement effectively increases our operational liability. I recommend: require Dedicated or Private deployment for this exception, and include a time-limited pilot with specific rollback criteria.

I'll draft suggested contract language if Marissa confirms ACME is willing to accept dedicated capacity and an exception term sheet.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security

Thanks for the quick turn, everyone — consolidated next steps for sales + product/legal: 

Decision proposal (for leadership approval):
- Offer ACME a 6-month pilot on Dedicated capacity (US-only) with enforced routing to model-x-us-v1 and allow_fallback=false.
- Pilot includes a one-time setup fee and a reserved capacity commitment.
- We will provide per-request audit logs and a documented operator-failover runbook (failover only by documented emergency process).
- Exception term sheet attached: exception_term_sheet.pdf.

What I need from you by EOD Friday: 
- Aditya: engineering estimate broken into init implementation (control plane + UI) and ops runbook + monitoring checklist (for the JIRA ticket INF-4217).
- Karthik: draft clause for the exception term sheet (liability, operator-failover, KMS expectations).
- Hannah/Laura: final approval to present the pilot to ACME legal and commercial team.

ACME is motivated to move quickly but will not sign if we cannot clearly explain availability tradeoffs. If we land this pilot it is a net-new Dedicated account and expands our footprint in manufacturing robotics, which is strategically important.

I'll open the HubSpot update and create the Jira ticket INF-4217 with the attached materials. Linking docs: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456/DEAL-8341, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4217, https://docsend.com/d/ACME-exception-term-sheet
